text:
maria (support): customer on tenant-8432 reporting sustained 502s from /v1/generate (hosted) starting ~12:45 UTC. customer says SDK retries pile up and they see partial streams then a reset. sample error: "upstream response timeout". asking for triage.
sam (sre): can you paste the request pattern and SDK version? is this streaming (http2) or non-streaming? any token sizes?
maria (support): streaming via SDK v1.2.0, http2 multiplexing, concurrency ~40-60 rps from their side, typical prompt ~700 tokens, max response ~1200. quick log excerpt: 
```
edge-proxy: 2026-06-12T12:46:01Z tenant=tenant-8432 level=warn upstream="10.0.4.12:8080" error="upstream response timeout"
edge-proxy: 2026-06-12T12:46:02Z tenant=tenant-8432 level=error connection=reset by peer
backend: 2026-06-12T12:45:59Z model-worker-7 oom_kill=false tail_latency_p50=18ms p95=450ms
```
also saw a short CPU spike on the edge plane (85%) and accept queue growth.
jordan (platform): looks like keepalive / connection churn related. Yesterday we had an ingress kernel upgrade that changed default tcp_keepalive_time. can we get proxy metrics (conn_open, conn_close, accept_queue) and upstream 5xx counters?
maria (support): attaching counters snapshot (pasted): conn_open +1200/min, conn_close +1185/min, 502_count +430 in 15m, 504_count +30.
ona (support): suggested workaround to customer: 1) disable streaming (use polling generate) 2) reduce concurrency to 10-15 for a few minutes 3) SDK: enable exponential backoff and jitter (>=200ms base). Customer applied 1 and 3, reporting fewer visible failures but still occasional 502s.
sam (sre): I can try to reproduce. share a minimal repro script?
maria (support): pasted python repro snippet they used: 
```python
# repro_stream.py
from redwood import RedwoodSDK
client = RedwoodSDK(api_key="REDACTED", streaming=True)
for i in range(50):
    client.generate_stream({"prompt":"x"*1500, "max_tokens":1200})
```
Note: they multiplex 50 concurrent streams.
ora (support): small note - their SDK v1.2.0 had known http2 windowing quirks; ask them to try SDK v1.2.3 patch that flips `h2_window_size` default.
jordan (platform): I'm looking at edge logs now. I see `RST_STREAM` from upstream workers at ~12:46:01 correlated with per-worker epoll waits >200ms. can eng-oncall check worker kernel backlog?
sam (sre): putting eng-oncall tag. suspecting socket buffer exhaustion causing resets under heavy multiplex. immediate mitigation: enable per-tenant connection pooling throttle and fallback to non-stream model variant for tenant-8432. deploy-bot: rollback not needed yet, but we can toggle feature flag.
deploy-bot: feature flip `tenant-pool-throttle-v2` scheduled to enable for tenant-8432 in ~2m.
maria (support): notified customer: applied throttle + recommended SDK patch and non-streaming fallback. customer asked for ETA on fix and worried about billing for the retry storm.
sam (sre): created internal issue INC-2026 and billing touchpoint. will capture retry counts and refund if spike due to our gateway behavior.
nona (support): triage checklist sent to eng: 1) reproduce with their concurrency locally 2) run with SDK v1.2.3 and http1 keepalive 60s 3) capture tcpdump + `ss -s` on worker during repro 4) inspect `epoll_wait` latencies and socket sndbuf usage 5) evaluate increasing H2 window or forcing http1 for streaming for now.
jordan (platform): quick notes from a micro-repro i ran with 30 concurrent streams: reproduced `RST_STREAM` after ~90s. stack: edge-proxy -> model-worker container -> grpc worker. adding `--http1-force=true` to edge-proxy eliminated resets in my run.
maria (support): customer update sent: workaround applied (non-streaming / SDK patch / throttle). they reported error rate dropped from ~7% to <1% in first 10 minutes. keeping on watch.
sam (sre): next steps: 1) get root cause from kernel/worker team (epoll backlog or socket exhaustion) 2) evaluate permanent config: increase per-worker fd limit and h2 window or keep http1 fallback for streaming-heavy tenants 3) billing review for retry charges 4) follow up with customer in 24h.
maria (support): will schedule follow-up and keep thread updated. tagging #incidents if we escalate. :thumbsup:
